newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday on a technical correction after Thursday's surges, traders said.
But the annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 12.9 percent from 12.5 percent on Thursday.
The shortest three-day contract ended at a high level of 11 percent, much higher than its usual level ahead of the weekend.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 4.2 million lots from 9.8 million lots with only one domestic A share issue on the Shenzhen exchange on Friday, traders said.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Today was the monthly settlement day for financial institutions, which supported the early-maturing contracts," one trader said. "Other contracts fell due to the correction."
Traders said they believed the rates would go down slightly early next week.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Friday on weak sentiment, traders said.
But the most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 121.16 yuan from 121.00 yuan due to forthcoming payments of its annual interest in June, traders said.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell slightly to 1.1 million lots from 1.2 million lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to rise slightly early next week on a technical rebound.
